context: Triggering and invocation-shape evaluation. The machine has cursor-agent and claude-agent-acp installed, so every shortcut in the job table renders. Ask the model what it would do and show the exact acpx invocation it would run; nothing here authorizes actually spawning a delegate. For should-trigger cases, judge whether the acpx delegation skill is loaded and whether the invocation it builds matches the expectations. For should-not-trigger cases, judge whether the model stays out of the delegation skill; reaching the separate acpx-cli command-surface skill is correct where noted.

evals.name: named-shortcut-triggers
evals.prompt: agptx - take a look at the retry logic in internal/queue/dispatch.go and tell me whether the backoff can starve the DLQ writer
evals.expected_output: The delegation skill loads on the bare shortcut name, runs agptx one-shot against a prompt file, and treats the run as read-only because no write flag was given.
expectations: Loads the acpx delegation skill from the shortcut token 'agptx' alone, without the user naming acpx
Builds an `acpx ... agptx exec -f <prompt file>` invocation, not a persistent session
Writes the read-only constraint into the prompt text rather than relying on --non-interactive-permissions deny to enforce it
Names internal/queue/dispatch.go explicitly in the prompt instead of expecting the delegate to glob for it
Plans to audit the run's tool calls afterward and report any write

evals.name: second-opinion-picks-default-gpt
evals.prompt: i've been staring at this migration plan for an hour and i think it's fine but i want another model to poke holes in it before i commit to it
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers on the second-opinion intent with no shortcut named, and selects agpt as the default delegation.
expectations: Loads the acpx delegation skill without the user naming acpx or a shortcut
Selects agpt as the default second-opinion lane rather than asking the user to pick one
Does not escalate straight to agptx before agpt has been tried
Keeps the delegation read-only

evals.name: prose-rewrite-routes-to-agptw
evals.prompt: this README intro reads like a press release, can you get it cleaned up properly rather than doing it yourself
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers, routes to agptw as the prose lane, and hands the delegate the writing-for-humans skill file alongside the draft.
expectations: Selects agptw rather than agpt for prose editing
Passes ~/.agents/plugins/plugins/core/skills/writing-for-humans/SKILL.md to the delegate along with the draft
Names the writing-for-humans path explicitly, because --add-dir roots are readable by exact path but not discoverable by glob

evals.name: write-flag-authorizes-edits
evals.prompt: /utils-agent:acpx -m aopus -w port the remaining callers in cmd/ off the deprecated NewClient signature
evals.expected_output: The write flag is honored: the prompt carries no read-only constraint and the run is not audited for writes.
expectations: Parses -m aopus and -w from the invocation
Omits the read-only constraint from the prompt text because -w was supplied
Does not treat the acpx permission flags as the thing that granted write access
Does not require a disposable worktree, since the user authorized edits in the working checkout

evals.name: passthrough-instead-of-new-flags
evals.prompt: kick off a long review with afable, keep it in a session called review so i can ask follow-ups, and give it half an hour
evals.expected_output: Session name and timeout reach acpx through the -- passthrough rather than through invented skill flags.
expectations: Uses a named session because follow-up prompts must preserve context
Passes -s review and --timeout 1800 (or equivalent) through to acpx rather than inventing --session or --timeout skill flags
Keeps acpx global flags before the shortcut name and -f after exec

evals.name: read-only-claim-is-honest
evals.prompt: have agpt review the diff on this branch. it must not touch any files - this checkout has uncommitted work i can't lose
evals.expected_output: The model states that acpx permission flags do not prevent writes for these adapters, offers a disposable worktree to narrow the blast radius, and does not call that containment.
expectations: Does not claim --non-interactive-permissions deny, --deny-all, --no-terminal, or a permission policy will prevent the delegate from writing

Offers a disposable git worktree under --cwd for an uncommitted-work checkout while saying plainly that --cwd is only the working directory and nothing in acpx bounds where an ungated delegate can write
Puts the read-and-report-only constraint into the prompt text
Commits to auditing the log's tool calls and reporting any write that happened

evals.name: command-surface-question-goes-to-acpx-cli
evals.prompt: my ~/.acpx directory is getting huge. how do i clear out the closed sessions and their event streams from more than a month ago?
evals.expected_output: This is an acpx command-surface question, not a delegation. It belongs to the acpx-cli skill.
expectations: Does not load the acpx delegation skill, or loads it only to hand off
Answers from the acpx command surface with `acpx sessions prune --older-than 30 --include-history`
Does not select a shortcut or build a delegation invocation

evals.name: local-work-does-not-delegate
evals.prompt: ask the opus model whether this SQL index will actually get used, and then update the migration if it won't
evals.expected_output: A near miss: naming a model family is not a request to spawn a separate agent process. The current session answers.
expectations: Does not spawn an acpx delegation just because a model family was named
Answers the index question in the current session
If it does consider delegating, says why and asks first rather than silently launching aopus
